dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Reduce the test_rubric_contains_* prose-verbatim assertions to canonical section anchors (or cover the new abstain/dedup/closed-parent rubric rules behaviorally via the plan-review-g7 eval fixtures) rather than pinning free-prose sentences.
evidence: search_files: 'covered-but-unverified' and 'DEDUP-AT-SOURCE' appear only in the rubric .md / generated guide / this test — no source-code consumer parses these tokens
Rule-5 litmus: a prose grep over an LLM instruction artifact that guards the author's wording is a change-detector, not a structural-boundary assertion (an LLM is not a non-human consumer)
dropped.finding: The four test_rubric_contains_* tests assert verbatim prose sentences from the LLM-facing reviewer rubric (plan_review_G7.md), not any parser-consumed contract token. An LLM is not a non-human consumer, and search confirms this rubric text is read by no code — so these are change-detectors that break on a behavior-preserving reword of the guidance with no change to observable review behavior. Free-prose assertions like 'never a finding', 'covered-but-unverified', 'ONLY a genuine contract contradiction or a provably required omission', and 'coached, never auto-blocked' pin the author's wording rather than the rubric's effect on review behavior (which is exercised only by the plan-review-g7 eval).
scenarios: A future editor reflows the FAIL-OPEN/DEDUP paragraph wording (same semantics) and these four tests fail spuriously despite unchanged review behavior.
